Where does this shortwave schedule come from?

From the EIBI shortwave database, compiled by Eike Bierwirth and rebuilt on ShortwaveHQ every day, with corrections from listeners and broadcasters where EIBI is out of date. The current season is B-26.

Why are shortwave schedules in UTC?

Broadcasts cross many time zones, so schedules use Coordinated Universal Time, which never changes for daylight saving. This page shows your local time next to each hour automatically; you can also use the UTC converter.

When does the shortwave schedule change?

Twice a year, on the last Sunday of March (A season) and of October (B season). The B-26 season runs until March 28, 2027.

What can I hear on shortwave right now?

Check the hour that matches the current UTC time on this page, or open On Air Now for a live list. In the evening, the 49 m and 41 m bands (around 6 and 7 MHz) are usually busiest; in daylight, try 25 m to 19 m (11.6 to 15.8 MHz).

How many shortwave stations are on the air?

The B-26 schedule lists 269 stations on 701 frequencies, broadcasting in 178 languages.
